D’ANGLETERRE IS SEARCHING FOR A FULL-TIME DOORMAN

At d’Angleterre, the guest experience begins before a guest even steps inside the hotel.

We are looking for a warm, confident and attentive Doorman to join our Front Office team. As one of the first people our guests meet and one of the last they see when they leave, you play an important role in creating the lasting impression they take with them.

This role is about much more than opening doors. You represent d’Angleterre through genuine hospitality, personal recognition and an ability to anticipate what each guest may need.

ABOUT THE JOB

As our Doorman, you will create seamless and personalised arrival and departure experiences while ensuring the hotel entrance operates smoothly.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Welcoming hotel, restaurant and event guests with warmth and genuine personal attention

• Recognising returning guests and anticipating individual needs

• Opening hotel and car doors, assisting with luggage and guiding guests to their destination

• Parking and retrieving guest vehicles safely and handling keys with care

• Coordinating taxis, transfers and guest movement with Concierge, Reception and the luggage team

• Staying informed about arrivals, departures, VIP guests and inhouse events to help personalise the experience

• Sharing relevant guest preferences and requests with colleagues to ensure seamless service

• Providing knowledgeable information about the hotel and Copenhagen

• Maintaining a welcoming, polished and safe hotel entrance

• Taking ownership of guest requests and consistently representing the service and discretion expected at d’Angleterre

ABOUT YOU

You have a natural ability to make people feel welcome. You are warm and approachable while remaining polished, professional and attentive to detail.

Experience from a luxury hotel or another high-end guest-facing environment is preferred, but your personality and instinct for hospitality are just as important.

You remain calm in a busy environment, communicate confidently in English and enjoy working as part of a team. Danish and other languages are an advantage, as is a good knowledge of Copenhagen.

A valid driving licence suitable for driving guest vehicles in Denmark is required, and you must be comfortable parking different types of vehicles.

The position includes flexible shifts across days, afternoons and weekends.

WE OFFER

You will join one of Copenhagen’s most iconic luxury hotels and become part of an ambitious team dedicated to creating exceptional and personalised guest experiences.

As Doorman, you hold a particularly visible place within that experience.

You are not simply standing at the entrance to d’Angleterre. You are representing it.

ABOUT HOTEL D’ANGLETERRE

For more than 265 years, Hotel d’Angleterre has welcomed guests in the heart of Copenhagen. Today, we continue to combine our heritage with an ambition to develop and set new standards for luxury hospitality.

We believe exceptional service is ultimately about how we make people feel. And often, that experience begins with the person at the door.

Are you an inspiring and hands-on leader with a passion for luxury hospitality, impeccable standards and creating exceptional guest experiences?

Hotel d’Angleterre is looking for an experienced Executive Housekeeping Manager to lead our Housekeeping Department and take overall responsibility for the presentation, care and continuous development of our guestrooms, suites and public areas.

About the role

As Executive Housekeeping Manager, you will be responsible for the overall leadership and operation of the Housekeeping Department. You will combine a strong operational presence with a continuous focus on the guest experience, quality, people development and efficiency.

You will create a respectful, motivated and high-performing team culture, while ensuring sound financial management, efficient operations and consistently exceptional standards throughout the hotel.

A key part of your role will be to uphold and continuously develop our Housekeeping standards, ensuring that every guestroom and public area reflects the quality and attention to detail expected at d’Angleterre. You will ensure that LQA requirements and our own service standards are translated into daily behaviours and consistently maintained through training, coaching, inspections and quality follow-up.

Beyond maintaining standards, you will take an active role in developing how we work. You will identify opportunities to improve the guest experience, protect the quality of our physical product and strengthen the efficiency and effectiveness of the department.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Leading, developing and inspiring the Housekeeping team, creating a culture of accountability, pride, collaboration and continuous learning

• Recruiting, onboarding, coaching and developing colleagues and future Housekeeping leaders

• Planning staffing and schedules in line with occupancy, arrivals, departures, events and operational demands

• Ensuring impeccable standards across guestrooms, suites, public areas and back-of-house spaces

• Taking ownership of the presentation, condition and continuous improvement of the Housekeeping product

• Ensuring thoughtful preparation for VIP arrivals, repeat guests, special occasions and individual guest preferences

• Leading ongoing training, coaching and quality follow-up, including LQA standards, room inspections and luxury service behaviours

• Establishing structured deep-cleaning and preventive maintenance programmes in close collaboration with Engineering

• Conducting regular quality inspections and translating guest feedback and quality results into meaningful improvements

• Owning the departmental budget and driving labour productivity, purchasing, inventory management and relevant operational KPIs, while protecting the quality of the guest experience

• Overseeing linen, uniforms, guest supplies and laundry service levels, ensuring the right balance of quality, availability and cost control

• Working closely with Front Office, Engineering and other departments to ensure arrival priorities, room readiness and special requests are seamlessly coordinated

• Promoting team well-being, safe and sustainable working practices and efficient ways of working

• Continuously reviewing processes and identifying opportunities to improve quality, productivity and the overall guest experience

About you

You have proven senior Housekeeping leadership experience, preferably from a five-star luxury hotel or a similarly high-end hospitality environment.

You are a visible and confident leader who enjoys being close to the operation and the team, while also having the ability to step back, identify opportunities and continuously develop the department.

You combine strong operational knowledge with warmth, structure and an exceptional eye for detail. You are comfortable making decisions, setting clear expectations and creating accountability, while leading with respect and genuine care for your team.

You have experience with team development, training, workforce planning, budgeting, labour productivity, inventory management and quality assurance. You communicate clearly, remain calm under pressure and enjoy working collaboratively across departments.

Most importantly, you understand that exceptional Housekeeping is not only about what a guest sees, but how the room and the experience make them feel.

Professional English is required, while Danish or other languages will be considered an advantage.

We offer

You will join one of Scandinavia's most iconic luxury hotels and take responsibility for a department that plays a defining role in the d’Angleterre experience.

Here, tradition and high standards go hand in hand with a genuine ambition to continuously evolve. You will have the opportunity to shape Housekeeping operations, develop people and processes, and contribute directly to the quality of the hotel and the experiences we create for our guests.

You will become part of an ambitious and professional environment where personalised service, development and mutual respect are at the heart of everything we do.

At Hotel d’Angleterre, we believe that exceptional luxury starts with the people behind it.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Stimuli-Triggered Nanoparticles and T-Cell Therapeutics for Improved Treatment of Malignant Brain Tumors - DTU Health Tech
jobs.description:
If you have a strong research interest in advanced drug delivery, cancer immunotherapy and the development of innovative treatments for brain cancer, this might be the right PhD position for you.

The aim of the PhD project is to develop a novel targeted drug delivery platform for the treatment of glioblastoma. The project combines genetically engineered CAR T cells with stimuli-responsive nanoparticles and in vitro and in vivo characterization the developed platform. 

As a PhD student you will be a part of the Pharmaceutical Technology group at DTU Health Tech. Find more information at www.healthtech.dtu.dk/research/research-sections/section-idun.

In the group, we are exploring and developing targeted and advanced delivery systems to be able to e.g. deliver small molecules, biologics and vaccines. The ultimate goals of these activities are to enhance the systemic uptake, to prevent and/or cure diseases. The group is part of the Drug Delivery and Sensing (IDUN) section at DTU Department of Health Technology. Furthermore, the PhD project is in close collaboration with researchers at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU), University of Copenhagen (UCPH) and Skåne University Hospital.

Responsibilities
Primarily, you will be working in the research area of nanoparticles, cancer immune therapy and brain delivery. 

The research tasks include: 

• Develop stimuli-sensitive nanoparticles and in vitro characterize these 
• Engineer CAR-T cells 
• In vitro cell characterization 
• In vivo studies to determine effect of the developed platforms.
The project will be carried out in close collaboration with colleagues from the IDUN section, SDU, UCPH and Skåne University Hospital.

Qualifications
The ideal candidate for the position will feature the following profile:

• Dynamic, independent, creative and goal-oriented
• Strong technical background in nanoparticle development
• Knowledge and hands-on experience with cell handling 
• Experience with immune therapy and in vivo studies 
• Capable of handling a multifaceted project with many stakeholders and collaborators
You are expected to have a background in areas related to pharmaceutical sciences/technology, chemistry or biomaterials. Furthermore, you are expected to be highly independent, self-motivated and enjoy collaboration in a multidisciplinary academic environment. Moreover, you should have the ability to drive the project forward and to set and achieve ambitious goals. You should also enjoy supervising and teaching BSc and MSc students. The project is highly interdisciplinary and we expect that you enjoy teamwork and are good at coordinating your work with your colleagues. 

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by Assoc. Prof. Line Hagner Nielsen and Assoc. Prof. Maria Ormhøj.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years.The position is a full-time position. Starting date is 1 April 2027 or according to mutual agreement. 

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Associate Prof. Line Hagner Nielsen, lihan@dtu.dk.

You can read more about DTU Health Tech at www.healthtech.dtu.dk/english.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 12 January 2027 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Health Tech engages in research, education, and innovation base on technical and natural science for the healthcare sector. The Healthcare sector is a globally expanding market with demands for the most advanced technological solutions. DTU Health Tech creates the foundation for companies to develop new and innovative services and products which benefit people and create value for society. DTU Health Techs expertise spans from imaging and biosensor techniques, across digital health and biological modelling, to biopharma technologies. The department has a scientific staff of about 210 persons, 140 PhD students and a technical/administrative support staff of about 160 persons, of which a large majority contributes to our research infrastructure and related commercial activities.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: PhD positions at the Cosmic Dawn Center
jobs.description:
The Cosmic Dawn Center (DAWN) at the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen, invites applications for up to three PhD positions. The positions are part of a dedicated research project funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF).

  DAWN is a Center of Excellence funded by the Danish National Research Foundation (DNRF) and is located in the Copenhagen area at the Niels Bohr Institute (NBI), University of Copenhagen and the Space division of the Danish Technical University (DTU-Space). In addition, DAWN has several associates at major research institutes across Europe, North America, and Australia. DAWN brings together experts in all aspects of early Universe research and is deeply involved in major existing and upcoming surveys with JWST and HST (e.g. SPURS, COSMOS3D, FRESCO, COSMOS-Web, RUBIES, BEACON, and CLUTCH), ALMA (e.g. CHAMPS), and Euclid (e.g. Cosmic Dawn Survey of the deep fields), as well as simulations. 

   

  The projects

  Up to three PhD positions are available at DAWN/NBI. Two are as part of the DFF Sapere Aude-funded project “Revealing Massive Stars at Cosmic Dawn” in Associate Professor Charlotte Mason’s group to work on both observational and theoretical projects on galaxy formation and reionization, including analysing data from the SPURS JWST survey. Applicants with interests and potential experience in any of galaxy formation, Lyman-alpha emission, atomic physics and radiative transfer, IGM/CGM evolution, AGN/LRDs, galaxy-dark matter connections, statistical inference, JWST NIRSpec spectroscopy, and comparing simulations to observations are strongly encouraged to apply.

  A third position is available to work with Professor Darach Watson’s group on early universe galaxies and black holes, including Little Red Dots using JWST.

  DAWN/NBI offers creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment, and strongly supports and encourages broad and open collaborations within the department for all prospective PhD fellows.

  Additional PhD positions may be available to work on specific projects at DAWN funded through individual group leadership grants with applications pending in December 2026. Applicants with research interests in any of the above DAWN research themes are strongly encouraged to apply. 

  Applicants to this position will be automatically considered for all available PhD positions at DAWN/NBI at the time of review.

   

  The PhD programme

  Depending on your level of education, you can undertake the PhD programme as either:

  Option A: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Option B: An up to five year full-time study programme within the framework of the integrated MSc and PhD programme (the 3+5 scheme), if you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree – but you have an education equivalent to a Danish bachelor's degree.

  ********************************************************************************

  Option A: Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme 

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. physics/astrophysics. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

   

  Terms of employment in the regular programme 
 Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for a maximum of 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment according to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Option B: Getting into a position on the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the integrated MSc and PhD programme 

  If you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree, you might be qualified for the integrated MSc and PhD programme, if you have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish bachelor´s degree. Here you can find out, if that is relevant for you: General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database. 

  Terms of the integrated programme
 To be eligible for the integrated scholarship, you are (or are eligible to be) enrolled at one of the faculty’s master programmes in Astrophysics at the Niels Bohr Institute.

  Students on the integrated programme will enroll as PhD students simultaneously with completing their enrollment in this MSc degree programme.

  The duration of the integrated programme is up to five years, and depends on the amount of credits that you have passed on your MSc programme. For further information about the study programme, please see:  www.science.ku.dk/phd, “Study Structures”.

  Until the MSc degree is obtained, (when exactly two years of the full 3+5 programme remains), the grant will be paid partly in the form of 48 state education grant portions (in Danish: “SU-klip”) plus salary for work (teaching, supervision etc.) totalling a workload of 150 working hours per year.
 A PhD grant portion is currently (2025) DKK 6.820 before tax.
 
 When you have obtained the MSc degree, you will transfer to the salary-earning part of the scholarship for a period of two years. At that point, the terms of employment and payment will be according to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Responsibilities and tasks in both PhD programmes

   	
• Complete and pass the MSc education in accordance with the curriculum of the MSc programme     (ONLY when you are attending the integrated MSc and PhD programme)

   	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision    	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project    

  We are looking for the following qualifications:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project 	
• Relevant publications 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Other relevant professional activities 	
• Curious mind-set with a strong interest in extragalactic astrophysics 	
• Good English language skills    

  ***************************************************************************

  Application and Assessment Procedure

  Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Cover letter (max. two pages) concisely outlining your research interests and motivation for applying to the PhD project, relevant research and educational experience. Explain what has shaped your research ambitions, why you wish to pursue a PhD, your relevant past work, and your future career goals.  	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position, any publications, and a list of up to 3 people who could be contacted for references. 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor or Master and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted.     

  Application deadline: 

  The deadline for applications is 22 December 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

   

  The further process 
 After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

  The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified and, if so, for which of the two models. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in early to mid February, 2027.

   

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD position, please contact the principal supervisor:

  Dr. Charlotte Mason, charlotte.mason@nbi.ku.dk

  or

  Prof. Darach Watson, darach@nbi.ku.dk

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

The Department of Computer Science at the University of Copenhagen (DIKU) invites applications for PhD positions in theoretical computer science and/or combinatorial optimization, tentatively commencing 1 July 2027 (but the starting date is negotiable).

  Description of the scientific environment

  The PhD students will be part of a world-leading research environment (currently ranked 11th worldwide in algorithms and complexity theory by CSrankings.org), with a strong presence at top-tier conferences like STOC, FOCS, and SODA, and also with publications in premier AI conferences like AAAI, IJCAI, and NeurIPS. We are home to the Basic Algorithms Research Copenhagen (BARC) centre (https://barc.ku.dk/), joint with the IT University of Copenhagen, and have extensive collaborations with the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) and with Lund University on the Swedish side of the Øresund Bridge, as well as with our many visitors. We aim to attract top talent from around the world to an ambitious, creative, collaborative, and fun environment. Using the power of mathematics, we strive to create fundamental breakthroughs in algorithms and complexity theory. While our focus in on theoretical research, we do have a track record of surprising algorithmic discoveries leading to major industrial applications.

  The University of Copenhagen was founded in 1479 and is the oldest and largest university in Denmark. It is often ranked as the best university in Scandinavia and consistently as one of the top places in Europe. Within computer science, it is ranked 2nd in the European Union by ShanghaiRanking.

  Further information about the Department of Computer Science and the Faculty of Science can be found at http://www.science.ku.dk/english/about-the-faculty/organisation/.

  Inquiries about the positions can be made to Mikkel Abrahamsen (miab@di.ku.dk), or Amir Yehudayoff (amye@di.ku.dk).

  Candidates interested in working with other faculty in the Algorithms and Complexity Section (https://di.ku.dk/english/staff/vip/researchers_ac/) are also encouraged to apply.

   

  Job description

  The positions are available for period of 3-5 years, depending on your current education level as discussed further below, and your key tasks as a PhD student at SCIENCE are to:

   	
• Manage and carry through your research project. 	
• Complete and pass the MSc education in accordance with the curriculum of the MSc programme (only if you are attending the integrated MSc and PhD programme).    	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approximately 30 ECTS (1/2 full-term equivalent). 	
• Teach and disseminate your research. 	
• Participate in research exchange by working at another research institution, preferably abroad, for a few months. 	
• Write scientific articles aimed at high-impact conferences and journals. 	
• Write and defend your PhD thesis on the basis of your research project.    

  Who are we looking for?

  To be eligible to apply for these positions, applicants need to have, or be about to obtain either a BSc or an MSc degree in computer science, mathematics, or a related field. The successful candidates are expected to have a strong background and passionate interest in mathematics and theoretical computer science, as demonstrated by excellent grades in relevant courses and publications in relevant internationally recognized conferences or journals such as SODA, STOC or FOCS. Problem solving skills and creativity are a must.

  Applicants need to be highly motivated for doctoral studies; should possess the ability to work independently and perform critical analysis, and also have good levels of communicative abilities and English language skills.

  The working language of the group is English, and knowledge of English is also fully sufficient to navigate life in Denmark in general. It might also be worth mentioning that Denmark routinely scores as the absolute top in rankings of quality of life such as, e.g., the OECD Better Life Index http://www.oecdbetterlifeindex.org .

   

  Principal supervisor will be associate professor Mikkel Abrahamsen, miab@di.ku.dk https://sites.google.com/view/mikkel-abrahamsen) at the Department of Computer Science (DIKU).

   

  The PhD programme

  Depending of your level of education, you can undertake the PhD programme as either:

  Option A: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Option B: An up to five year full-time study programme within the framework of the integrated MSc and PhD programme (the 3+5 scheme), if you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree – but you have an education equivalent to a Danish bachelors´s degree.

  ********************************************************************************

  Option A: Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme 

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. [relevant educations]. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment in the regular programme 
 Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

   

  Option B: Getting into a position on the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the integrated MSc and PhD programme 

  If you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree, you might be qualified for the integrated MSc and PhD programme, if you have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish bachelor´s degree. Here you can find out, if that is relevant for you: General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.  

  Terms of the integrated programme
 To be eligible for the integrated scholarship, you are (or are eligible to be) enrolled at one of the faculty’s master programmes in computer science.

  Students on the integrated programme will enroll as PhD students simultaneously with completing their enrollment in this MSc degree programme.

  The duration of the integrated programme is up to five years, and depends on the amount of credits that you have passed on your MSc programme. For further information about the study programme, please see: www.science.ku.dk/phd, “Study Structures”.

  Until the MSc degree is obtained, (when exactly two years of the full 3+5 programme remains), the grant will be paid partly in the form of 48 state education grant portions (in Danish: “SU-klip”) plus salary for work (teaching, supervision etc.) totalling a workload of 150 working hours per year.
  

  A PhD grant portion is currently (2027) DKK 7,608 before tax.
 
 When you have obtained the MSc degree, you will transfer to the salary-earning part of the scholarship for a period of two years. At that point, the terms of employment and payment will be according to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Responsibilities and tasks in both PhD programmes

   	
• Complete and pass the MSc education in accordance with the curriculum of the MSc programme (ONLY when you are attending the integrated MSc and PhD programme)    	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision    	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project   ***************************************************************************

  Application and Assessment Procedure

   Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Curriculum vitae. 	
• Brief statement as to why the applicant wishes to conduct doctoral studies, including a description of the applicant's qualifications and interests. 	
• Diploma and transcripts of records (BSc and MSc), including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Other information for consideration, e.g., BSc/MSc thesis or research publications.   Application deadline: 

  The deadline for applications is Sunday, 3 January 2027 at 23:59 GMT +2.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

  The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified and, if so, for which of the two models. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact the principal supervisor.

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

Postdoctoral fellow in gut metabolism through the NORPOD program
Are you interested in stem cell biology, gut metabolism, neuroendocrinology and can you contribute to the development of the project 'One receptor, two hormones'? Then the Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics, and DANDRITE - The Danish Research Institute of Translational Neuroscience - Aarhus University, Denmark, invites you to apply for a 2,5 year position.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a 2,5–year position from May/June 2027 or as soon possible thereafter.

Job description
This position will involve conducting and analysing experiments to understand the impact of glucagon receptor duplication on glucose handling and behaviours in zebrafish. As well as how this relates to the GLP-1/glucagon pathway in mammals.

The project entails:

• Experiments involving zebrafish genetic and dietary models
• Experiments involving mouse genetic and dietary models
• Generation of germ-free and conventionalized zebrafish models
• in vivo imaging of gut motility, enteric neuronal activity, and immune responses (Confocal microscope and Light Sheet Fluorescence microscopy)
• RNA-sequencing and in-situ hybridization
Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Contributing to the publication of scientific papers by conducting planned experiments toward understanding how inflammation and the enteric nervous system affect each other. Contribute to an inclusive, cooperative, and affirmative culture within the group.

Your profile
Applicants should hold a PhD in Molecular biology or similar.

Essential

• Experience and a track record in zebrafish or mice research
• Excellent communication skills in English and the ability to work collaboratively
• A valid animal experimentation certificate
• Experience with transcriptomics or metabolomics, approaches
Desirable  

• Experience with imaging, especially in vivo imaging
• Experience with intestinal disease models
• Record of first-author publications or preprints
• Experience with inflammatory models
• Experience with metabolism

Who we are
NORPOD is a collaborative postdoctoral program of the Nordic EMBL Partnership for Molecular Medicine. The partnership is a network of four national research centers across the Nordics and the European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL), with complementary research expertise at the forefront of molecular medicine research. With the NORPOD program, the Nordic EMBL Partnership aims to foster the next generation of researchers in molecular medicine by implementing joint postdoctoral research projects to nurture strong competences and research excellence. DANDRITE is a Danish research center dedicated to understanding the brain and nervous system. DANDRITE is part of the Nordic EMBL Partnership for Molecular Medicine and is hosted by Aarhus University at the Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics. The Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics is part of the Faculty of Natural Sciences, Aarhus University and comprises research within the areas of Plant Molecular Biology, Neurobiology, RNA Biology and Innovation, Protein Science, Cellular Health, Intervention and Nutrition. There are currently 75 full time scientific staff and 95 PhD students. The department is responsible for two educations: Molecular Biology and Molecular Medicine with a yearly uptake of 160 students in total. Please refer to http://mbg.au.dk/ for further information about The Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics and to https://nat.au.dk/ and http://www.au.dk/ for information on Faculty of Natural Sciences and Aarhus University, respectively.

What we offer
The department/centre offers:

• a well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment
• an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators
• a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
• a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities
• a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance
Place of work and area of employment
The successful candidate will be employed at DANDRITE, Aarhus University, Denmark. The project is a collaborative effort between DANDRITE and the Institute for Molecular Medicine Finland (FIMM), University of Helsinki, and therefore includes research stays in Helsinki, Finland, of varying duration during the project period.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Gilles Vanwalleghem, gilles.vanwalleghem@mbg.au.dk or Arafath Kaja Najumudeen arafath.najumudeen@helsinki.fi 

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 31 January 2027.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

At the Faculty of Natural Science at Aarhus University, we strive to support our scientific staff in their career development. We focus on competency development and career clarification and want to make your opportunities transparent. On our website, you can find information on all types of scientific positions, as well as the entry criteria we use when assessing candidates. You can also read more about how we can assist you in your career planning and development.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

About Aarhus University

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment for its 37,500 students, including PhD students, and has 9,000 employees (full-time equivalents) and an annual revenue of EUR 1.2 billion. Learn more at international.au.dk

At Sumary, we are rebuilding finance from first principles. In short, we are creating the AI operating system for accounting work. Founded in 2025, Sumary is already used by some of the largest accounting firms in the world, including Deloitte, Grant Thornton and Baker Tilly, and the products we ship will define how finance teams work in the coming decade.

We have raised $29m, including the largest seed round ever in the Nordics, from Singular, byFounders, Partech and Tenity, and angels including Tuomas Artman (Linear), Morten Primdahl (Zendesk), Steve Anavi (Qonto), Stanislas Polu (Dust), Steffen Tjerrild (Synthesia), Jannick Malling (Public) and Ben Freeman (Omnea).

Our engineers are also our product managers and designers. You talk to customers, understand their pain points, design the best solution and ship it to a standard that sets the bar for the industry. You are confident owning features end to end, from the data model to the last pixel of the interface.

AI writes most of our code, so producing code is no longer the bottleneck. Judgment is: deciding what is worth building, and making it excellent. Just because something takes half a day to build doesn't mean it should exist.

We are a small team of full-stack generalists, TypeScript end to end, and product comes first in everything we build. What unites us is a deep care for craft, fast execution and the discipline to say no. We are looking for experienced engineers who thrive on autonomy and individual responsibility.

We have offices in Copenhagen and London. Copenhagen is our engineering hub, and this role is based there.

**Come help define and build the future of finance.

**What you'll do

• Work closely with founders and customers, and turn what you hear into the right solution, which is often not the one they asked for

• Build new user-facing features end to end, with beautiful and scalable UI components

• Obsessively improve performance, so every interaction feels instant, even for our largest accounting firms

• Use what you built the way a customer would, and polish it until it is right before it ships

• Delete by default: push back on scope, on features we shouldn't build and on anything that feels off

• When an agent gets something wrong, fix the tooling so it doesn't happen again for anyone

What we're looking for

• 5+ years building customer-facing products at a company known for the quality of its software

• Deep fluency in TypeScript and React, and confidence across the full stack: Node.js, Postgres and the data model underneath

• Product obsession and a good eye for design: you care about UX, speed and polish. You notice the slow interaction, the awkward empty state and the setting nobody needs, and you fix them without being asked

• A track record of shipping complete features end to end, not only incremental work

• Comfort working without a product manager. You would rather talk to the customer yourself

• High ownership: you take a problem from start to finish and care about how it lands

• You know the difference between extra effort and meaningful quality

• You build AI-first, directing agents through the implementation while you own the judgment

Nice to have

• Experience as one of the first engineers at a startup that went on to scale

• Interfaces you designed yourself, not only built

• Experience with financial and ledger data

Our stack

TypeScript end to end: React and Next.js, Node.js, Postgres and Supabase, Temporal, Modal and our AI service layers. We don't expect you to have used all of it.

Applying

Along with your CV, send us something you built that you are proud of, and one thing in a product you use every day that you would fix.
